refs.name: Squam Lake (the archetype)
refs.blurb: The reference point. ≤$2.5M buys no usable compound here — but see the live 159 Rt-113 assemblage listings.

lakes.name: Kezar Lake
lakes.blurb: The truest Squam analog: oligotrophic, White Mtn backdrop, hushed. Thin market — and a live 16.6-ac Narrows parcel just surfaced.

lakes.name: Seymour Lake
lakes.blurb: Best odds of executing: oligotrophic, invasive-free, wakesports zone, compound-grade comps ~$1.25M.

lakes.name: Raquette Lake
lakes.blurb: Great Camp birthplace; wild bays, attainable entries, APA levers for a cabin cluster.

lakes.name: Big Moose Lake
lakes.blurb: Dark-timber old camps, near-zero ramp traffic. Two live listings: $1.2M boat-access and $1.1M road-access.

lakes.name: Merrymeeting Lake
lakes.blurb: Spring-fed clear, no big public ramp — quietest archetype water near the city.

lakes.name: Great East Lake
lakes.blurb: Secchi ~10 m. Inventory currently dry (one pending camp) — set alerts; cyanobacteria counts are the watch item.

lakes.name: Caspian Lake
lakes.blurb: Greensboro — the NEK's Squam-in-miniature. A rare $2.25M north-shore estate parcel is live now.

lakes.name: Maidstone Lake
lakes.blurb: State-forest ring, loons, one dirt road — the most Trout-Lake-WI place in New England.

lakes.name: Upper Saranac Lake
lakes.blurb: The NY Squam. ≤$2.5M buys one camp, not a compound — tour Panther Cove to calibrate.

lakes.name: Upper Chateaugay Lake
lakes.blurb: The value arbitrage: clear, cold, sleepy. $599K buys an 868-ft private cove.

lakes.name: Piseco Lake
lakes.blurb: Best drive-to-wildness ratio on the list; Forest Preserve ring, thin inventory.

lakes.name: Webb Lake
lakes.blurb: Mount Blue / Tumbledown wildness; the build-from-scratch canvas ($985K parcel live).

lakes.name: Newfound Lake
lakes.blurb: PROMOTED to Tier 2: world-class clarity and now real inventory — the $2.6M ten-room Kelby lodge plus $799K–$1.5M owned waterfront. Watch the spiny water flea.

lakes.name: Conway Lake
lakes.blurb: Sleeper: conserved eastern shore, tiny launch, cheaper than its neighbors; $1.25M camp live.

lakes.name: Thompson Lake
lakes.blurb: Archetype water, frontage drought continues — only access-rights homes live; set an alert.

lakes.name: Embden Pond
lakes.blurb: Cheapest clear water found: camps in the $400Ks; two live sub-$450K options.

lakes.name: Echo Lake (Charleston)
lakes.blurb: Clearest Secchi in the VT dataset (8.8 m); pair with Seymour. Current entry pending.

lakes.name: Lake Willoughby
lakes.blurb: Spectacular fjord; frontage scarce — but the live combo ($929K 8BR waterfront lodge + LaCross parcels) is Vermont's best compound math.

lakes.name: Lake Bonaparte
lakes.blurb: Islands, granite, generational camps; compound money goes far.

lakes.name: Chazy Lake
lakes.blurb: Clear, cold, sparse under Lyon Mtn; $265K entry live now.

lakes.name: Great Averill Pond
lakes.blurb: The NEK's best-kept secret — oligotrophic, forested, near-zero market (Quimby Country sold).

lakes.name: Mooselookmeguntic (edge)
lakes.blurb: Truest Trout Lake analog east of Wisconsin — 45 min over the drive line. Remarkable value.

lakes.name: Rangeley Lake (edge)
lakes.blurb: Classic ski-camp town, over the drive cap; only if the rule softens.

lakes.name: Silver Lake (Madison)
lakes.clarity: Oligotrophic (NHDES/UNH LLMP); high transparency, active association monitoring
lakes.motors: Unrestricted power/ski; PWC banned 2000; houseboats prohibited
lakes.blurb: Quiet forested White-Mtn-edge archetype: clear water, ski-legal, jetski-free, real camps; compound via 2-3-parcel assembly is realistic.

lakes.name: Lake Wentworth
lakes.clarity: Oligotrophic (NHDES/Wentworth Watershed Assoc); consistently clear
lakes.blurb: Big, clear, PWC-free, wooded shores with islands; Wolfeboro amenities 5 min; frontage trades but compounds rare.

lakes.name: Pleasant Lake (New London)
lakes.clarity: Oligotrophic, excellent clarity (NHDES VLAP)
lakes.blurb: Deep, gin-clear, Kearsarge backdrop, 4-hour drive; tradeoff is scarce, expensive frontage on a smaller lake.

lakes.name: Highland Lake (Stoddard)
lakes.clarity: Mesotrophic (NHDES VLAP N+S stations); decent clarity, slight tea stain
lakes.motors: Unrestricted; ski common; no PWC ban listed
lakes.blurb: Wildest Monadnock big-lake: 7 miles of largely conserved forest, loons, cheap camps; water good-not-gin-clear.

lakes.name: Spofford Lake
lakes.clarity: Oligotrophic-leaning, clear (NHDES 2024 VLAP; watershed plan)
lakes.motors: 40 mph day/20 night; ski culture strong
lakes.blurb: Closest passing lake to NYC; deep, clear, ski-friendly; tradeoff: fully ringed cottage road, little wild shore.

lakes.name: Ossipee Lake
lakes.clarity: Oligotrophic, sandy-bottomed (Ossipee Lake Alliance/NHDES monitoring)
lakes.blurb: Huge clear sandy lake plus quiet bays (Broad/Leavitt/Berry); caveat: weekend sandbar party scene and campgrounds.

lakes.name: Lake Winnisquam
lakes.clarity: Oligotrophic per NHDES table; watershed plan active; good clarity
lakes.blurb: NH's 4th-largest, ski-perfect and affordable; Ferry Point 13BR lodge = instant compound; south end is busy Rt-3 corridor.

lakes.name: Goose Pond (Canaan)
lakes.clarity: Oligo/mesotrophic, clear (GPLA/NHDES VLAP)
lakes.motors: Ski legal; PWC banned 1989; Narrows no-wake
lakes.blurb: Forested, jetski-free sleeper near Hanover; caveat: deep winter drawdown (2024 dam-work year extreme) and fewer services.

lakes.name: Nubanusit Lake
lakes.clarity: Oligotrophic, deep coldwater; among region's clearest (NHDES VLAP)
lakes.blurb: Trout-Lake-grade clarity, Harris-Center-conserved forest, 4 hours out — but frontage almost never trades; zero listings now.

lakes.name: Little Squam Lake
lakes.clarity: Shares Squam's oligotrophic clear system
lakes.motors: Ski legal; PWC banned 1988; channel no-wake
lakes.blurb: Size-exception justified: full boat access to Big Squam; watch = price and sub-450 acreage; Phase-0 homes exist.

lakes.name: Lake Umbagog
lakes.clarity: Mesotrophic, shallow, tannin-tinted; wild watershed (NWR)
lakes.motors: Motorboating permitted incl. refuge waters; ski legal
lakes.blurb: True wilderness (eagles, refuge shoreline) at edge-drive 7:00; scarce private frontage, stained shallow water; exceptional-fit override.

lakes.name: First Connecticut Lake
lakes.clarity: Cold, clear oligotrophic salmon water (NHDES trend reporting)
lakes.motors: Unrestricted; ski legal though water stays cold
lakes.blurb: Spectacular timber-country lake; edge 7:05 drive, thin camp inventory, short cold season — exceptional-fit watch only.

lakes.name: Lake Sunapee
lakes.clarity: Oligotrophic, very clear (NHDES; color 5)
lakes.blurb: Water is superb but harbor/regatta scene reads borderline-busy and $2.5M buys one house, never a compound.

lakes.name: Lovell Lake
lakes.clarity: Oligotrophic; avg Secchi 6.3 m (AWWA)
lakes.motors: Ski legal; no PWC ban listed
lakes.blurb: Surprisingly clear Wakefield sleeper; watch: AWWA phosphorus/cyano-frequency project and Rt-109/village edge.

lakes.name: Bow Lake
lakes.clarity: Mesotrophic, decent clarity; episodic cyanobacteria advisories (NHDES issued/removed)
lakes.blurb: Right size/drive/ski culture; watch item is recurring short cyanobacteria advisories and busier southern-NH feel.

lakes.name: Lake Waukewan
lakes.clarity: Oligo/mesotrophic; Meredith water supply with formal cyanobacteria response plan (2025)
lakes.blurb: Pretty, jetski-free, near Squam; watch: drinking-water-supply politics and active cyano monitoring plan.

lakes.name: Mascoma Lake
lakes.clarity: Mesotrophic, moderate clarity; variable milfoil documented (NHDES)
lakes.blurb: Shaker-village charm 15 min from Dartmouth; watch: milfoil history, I-89/rail-trail adjacency, colored water.

lakes.name: Pine River Pond
lakes.clarity: Mesotrophic, low color (NHDES table)
lakes.blurb: Wooded, jetski-free, honest camp lake; watch: dense small-lot ring, winter drawdown, limited wow-factor.

lakes.name: Little Lake Sunapee
lakes.clarity: Mesotrophic, good clarity (LLSPA monitoring)
lakes.blurb: Quiet New London alternative when Pleasant is unobtainable; watch: barely 471 ac and near-zero inventory.

lakes.name: Parker Pond
lakes.clarity: Oligo-meso; 2021 avg Secchi 8.2 m (hist 7.4), TP 4.8 ppb (30MRWA)
lakes.motors: No HP cap; ski-legal (CMR ch.13 §07 absent)
lakes.blurb: 1,500+ quiet acres, 8 m water, one restricted launch, loons, conserved headlands — Squam energy with live inventory.

lakes.name: Echo Lake (Fayette)
lakes.clarity: 2024 avg Secchi 7.2 m (hist 6.6), TP 6.2 ppb (30MRWA)
lakes.motors: No restrictions (10-hp 'Echo Lake' is Mt. Desert's)
lakes.blurb: Deep, clear, wooded Fayette water with YMCA camp heritage; affordable frontage; ideal ski loops.

lakes.name: Lake St. George
lakes.clarity: Oligotrophic; 'crystal clear' (state park guide); salmon water
lakes.blurb: Spring-fed, island-dotted, state-park anchored, Liberty prices: camp $395K, lots under $120K. Best value archetype.

lakes.name: Peabody Pond
lakes.clarity: Avg Secchi 8.0 m, low P (LEA 2022); oligotrophic
lakes.blurb: Closest truly pristine water: 8 m clarity, forested, no commercial anything. Inventory rare — patience or assemblage.

lakes.name: Moose Pond
lakes.clarity: Main basin avg Secchi 7.7 m (LEA 2022); stable; no invasives
lakes.blurb: Three basins under Pleasant Mtn; classic kids-camp water (Winona/Wyonegonic). Tradeoff: ski-area base traffic.

lakes.name: Pleasant Lake (Otisfield)
lakes.clarity: DEP 'excellent' class; spring-fed; high transparency
lakes.blurb: Otisfield's quiet spring-fed gem; Seeds of Peace camp proves compound format. Tradeoff: tight inventory.

lakes.name: Clearwater Pond
lakes.clarity: Oligotrophic, 129 ft deep, wild lake trout; famously transparent
lakes.blurb: Franklin County's clearest big pond; forested, lightly developed. Tradeoff: small market, few services.

lakes.name: Panther Pond
lakes.clarity: 2022 avg Secchi 7.0 m; oligo-meso, 30-yr stable (RWPA)
lakes.blurb: Camp Agawam water: clear, wooded, 25 min off the pike. Tradeoff: Raymond growth pressure.

lakes.name: Porter Lake
lakes.clarity: Secchi 8.5–9.0 m 2017–21 (Porter Lake Assn); healthy
lakes.blurb: Nine-meter water almost nobody knows; native lakers. Tradeoffs: 527 ac, remote-feeling, micro market.

lakes.name: Highland Lake (Bridgton)
lakes.clarity: Avg Secchi 7.4 m (LEA 2022); mesotrophic
lakes.blurb: Clear, islanded, 16-mi shoreline; north half quiet. Tradeoff: village beach/downtown at south end.

lakes.name: Sheepscot Pond
lakes.clarity: TP 5–10 ppb, stable Secchi, no blooms ever (SLA/DEP); 150 ft deep
lakes.blurb: Big, deep, healthy Palermo water with fish hatchery pedigree. Tradeoff: plainer shoreline market.

lakes.name: Long Pond (Belgrade)
lakes.clarity: 2024 Secchi 5.3–5.6 m, 'good all season' (7 Lakes Alliance)
lakes.blurb: Deep, mountain-framed Belgrade classic; Castle Island charm. Tradeoff: summer boat traffic.

lakes.name: Maranacook Lake
lakes.clarity: 'One of the cleanest in Maine' (wiki); deep 118-ft south basin
lakes.blurb: Clean two-basin lake, easy Augusta logistics. Tradeoff: heavier year-round development.

lakes.name: Pocasset Lake
lakes.clarity: 2024 avg Secchi 6.16 m (hist 5.7); meso, stable (30MRWA)
lakes.blurb: Wayne village charmer, quiet and clear. Tradeoff: modest 600 acres for serious cruising.

lakes.name: Crescent Lake
lakes.clarity: 2022 avg Secchi 6.8 m; oligo-meso (RWPA)
lakes.blurb: Panther's connected twin; clear, calmer, camp-lined. Tradeoff: smaller water, Rt 85 exposure.

lakes.name: Great Pond (Belgrade)
lakes.clarity: 2024 Secchi 5.7 m, good season (7LA); minor June scums
lakes.blurb: The 'On Golden Pond' sea: huge cruising range, island camps. Tradeoff: liveliest Belgrade social scene.

lakes.name: Crawford Pond (Union)
lakes.clarity: 'Above average' quality; 57 ft deep; 100-Acre Island preserve
lakes.blurb: Midcoast sleeper with preserved island and clean water. Tradeoff: small, low turnover.

lakes.name: Keoka Lake
lakes.clarity: Avg Secchi 6.8 m (LEA 2022); meso
lakes.blurb: Waterford village postcard, quiet and clear. Tradeoff: just clears the size bar.

lakes.name: Square Pond
lakes.clarity: Meso, decent clarity (LSM); no bloom history
lakes.blurb: Closest qualifying Maine water to NYC; solid ski pond. Tradeoff: dense camp shoreline, weekend buzz.

lakes.name: Pemaquid Pond
lakes.clarity: Meso, mid-4s m Secchi (LSM); no chronic blooms
lakes.blurb: Long, quiet, oyster-country lake near Damariscotta. Tradeoff: clarity a notch below the leaders.

lakes.name: Wilson Lake (Wilton)
lakes.clarity: Meso-clear; 88 ft deep, wild salmonids (FOWL)
lakes.blurb: Deep, tidy Wilton lake with active friends group. Tradeoff: town at south end, modest acreage.

lakes.name: Lake Wesserunsett
lakes.clarity: Long-term Secchi 5.9 m; TP 8 ppb 'warrants concern' (LWA 2017)
lakes.blurb: Lakewood Theater lake; roomy and affordable. Tradeoff: phosphorus creeping toward bloom threshold.

lakes.name: Megunticook Lake
lakes.clarity: Clear meso; monitored since 1975 (MWA); no invasives
lakes.blurb: Camden Hills backdrop, Fernald's Neck preserve — the prettiest water here. Caveat: 6:45 drive, Camden pricing.

lakes.name: Damariscotta Lake
lakes.clarity: Meso ~5 m; Aug 2024 cyanotoxin advisory (south arm), cleared on retest
lakes.blurb: 14 miles of island-strewn midcoast water, alewife runs. Caveat: episodic localized cyanobacteria advisories.

lakes.name: Richardson Lakes
lakes.clarity: Secchi 4.5–7.5 m; 'no significant health concerns,' sparse development (RLHT 2024)
lakes.blurb: Wildest big water in scope; loon wilderness. Caveats: 7:00 drive, mostly leased timberland frontage.

lakes.name: Swan Lake
lakes.clarity: Clear salmon lake; oligo-meso (LSM)
lakes.blurb: State-park lake above Belfast; 350 camps, honest prices. Caveats: drive edge, dam-level politics history.

lakes.name: Trickey Pond
lakes.clarity: Avg Secchi 9.7 m (LEA 2022) — clearest in region
lakes.blurb: Caribbean-clear outlier. Caveat: 315 acres — under size bar, tight ski loops, tiny inventory.

lakes.name: Alford Lake
lakes.clarity: Clear oligo-meso (LSM); Alford Lake Camp water
lakes.blurb: Hope's clean, low-key lake with camp pedigree. Caveats: modest size, thin public data and inventory.

lakes.name: Messalonskee (Snow Pond)
lakes.clarity: 2024 Secchi 4.5 m, 'good all season' (7LA)
lakes.blurb: Nine miles of cruising water, cheapest big-lake frontage in Belgrades. Caveats: mid clarity, busy Oakland end.

lakes.name: Mousam Lake
lakes.clarity: Recovered: delisted from impaired 2006; clarity +3 ft vs 1990s (EPA)
lakes.blurb: Closest-in option with real depth. Caveats: 700-home shoreline, restoration-era water still mid-pack.

lakes.name: Blue Mountain Lake
lakes.clarity: Famously clear oligo/mesotrophic; 100-ft holes, trout/salmon water
lakes.motors: NYS default (45 day, 5mph <100 ft); ski legal; launches limited to <20-ft boats
lakes.blurb: The archetype: island-dotted, mostly private shore, museum-quiet hamlet; verges t1 whenever a camp actually lists.

lakes.name: Lower Saranac Lake
lakes.clarity: Mesotrophic, good clarity; island-and-ledge water
lakes.motors: NYS default; ski legal; locks connect Middle/Oseetah
lakes.blurb: Fifty-island beauty, state campsite culture keeps shores wild; Pinehurst enclave offers a real compound seed.

lakes.name: Schroon Lake
lakes.clarity: Mesotrophic, Grade B, Secchi ~5 m
lakes.blurb: Big, clean, closest true ski lake; tradeoff is summer hamlet bustle and faint Northway hum on west shore.

lakes.name: Brant Lake
lakes.clarity: Clear mesotrophic; active milfoil control (ProcellaCOR)
lakes.blurb: Quiet forested sleeve of water north of Lake George glitz; strong camp stock, milfoil program is the caveat.

lakes.name: Skaneateles Lake
lakes.clarity: Ultra-oligotrophic Syracuse AA supply; Secchi ~8 m
lakes.motors: NYS default; ski legal; watershed rules govern shoreline/septic
lakes.blurb: Caribbean-clear but pastoral, pricey, and watershed-regulated; honest fit only if clarity outranks wilderness feel.

lakes.name: Lake Pleasant
lakes.clarity: Clear mesotrophic (CSLAP-monitored)
lakes.blurb: Speculator's home water: mountains, sand, short drive; Camp-of-the-Woods end lively, southwest shore quiet.

lakes.name: Sacandaga Lake (Speculator)
lakes.clarity: Clear mesotrophic; 90 ft deep
lakes.blurb: Pleasant's wilder twin: Forever-Wild shoreline stretches, islands, Moffitt Beach campground; closest credible compound water to NYC.

lakes.name: Lake Clear
lakes.clarity: Mesoligotrophic; Secchi avg ~4.6 m (to 6.9)
lakes.motors: No special restriction; NYS default; ski practical
lakes.blurb: Lives up to its name: sand, spring-fed clarity, St. Regis canoe country next door; caveat—adjacent regional airport, near-zero inventory.

lakes.name: Indian Lake
lakes.clarity: Mesotrophic, clear with light stain; CSLAP-monitored
lakes.blurb: Fourteen wild miles, state island campsites, Sabael camp colony; dam-controlled winter drawdown is the honest tradeoff.

lakes.name: Paradox Lake
lakes.clarity: Clear mesotrophic
lakes.motors: NYS default; ski fine in main basin
lakes.blurb: Sleepy two-basin water over the hill from Schroon; Rt 74 touches north shore, otherwise deep-forest quiet.

lakes.name: Long Lake
lakes.clarity: Mesotrophic; shallow (13-ft avg) Raquette River flow-through, light tea
lakes.motors: NYS default; ski/cruise culture, seaplane base
lakes.blurb: Fjord-like 14-mile cruise water with affordable frontage; river current, wind and stain keep it below the clarity elite.

lakes.name: Millsite Lake
lakes.clarity: Oligotrophic; Secchi 7.0 m avg (to 9.9)
lakes.motors: NYS default; ski legal, no houseboats
lakes.blurb: The Indian River sleeper: genuinely oligotrophic, granite-and-pine shores, tiny tight market; clarity rivals anything on this list.

lakes.name: Loon Lake (Chestertown)
lakes.clarity: Mesoligotrophic; Secchi ~3.7 m
lakes.blurb: Island-dotted, close, decent water; smaller basin and denser cottages mean one busy-Saturday tradeoff.

lakes.name: Loon Lake (Franklin Co.)
lakes.clarity: Mesotrophic, moderately clear
lakes.blurb: Faded Gilded-Age resort lake, quiet and cheap for its size; watch the contested golf-course redevelopment next door.

lakes.name: Canada Lake
lakes.clarity: Deep (70-ft mean), cold, clear trout water
lakes.blurb: Closest qualifying lake to Midtown, deep and clear into West/Green lakes; caveat—small century-old lots, compound assembly hard.

lakes.name: Sylvia Lake
lakes.clarity: Marble-basin spring water; locally billed clearest in NY
lakes.blurb: Size-exception candidate: swimming-pool clarity over white marble; only 317 acres, cottage-ringed, listings rare.

lakes.name: Keuka Lake
lakes.clarity: Oligo-mesotrophic, clean; KLA-monitored
lakes.blurb: Cleanest crooked lake in wine country; caveat—vineyard-pastoral not forested-wild, dense cottages, fast-moving market.

lakes.name: Fourth Lake (Fulton Chain)
lakes.clarity: Mesotrophic, clear
lakes.blurb: Honest verdict on the main chain: clear and handsome but Old Forge tourist wake culture; buy here for convenience, not Squam.

lakes.name: Cranberry Lake
lakes.clarity: Tea-stained Oswegatchie water, low-nutrient but brown
lakes.blurb: Wildest big lake in NY—75% state shoreline; caveats are real: dark water, long drive, thin hamlet market.

lakes.name: Seventh Lake (Fulton Chain)
lakes.clarity: Mesotrophic, clear; wilder upper chain
lakes.blurb: Quietest motorized link of the chain, state-forest south shore; caveat—Rt 28 noise and a micro market.

lakes.name: Otsego Lake
lakes.clarity: Deep mesotrophic 'Glimmerglass'; cyanobacteria blooms recurring since 2022
lakes.blurb: Closest big deep lake, estate shorelines; caveat—late-summer HAB advisories now near-annual plus Cooperstown tourist churn.

lakes.name: Lower Chateaugay Lake
lakes.clarity: Late-mesotrophic; Secchi ~2.3 m
lakes.motors: NYS default; navigable to Upper via Narrows
lakes.blurb: Cheap frontage and Narrows access to profiled Upper; caveat—clarity clearly a notch below, buy Upper first.

lakes.name: Osgood Pond
lakes.clarity: Tea-stained (55 Pt-Co); Secchi ~2.5 m, stable mesotrophic
lakes.blurb: White Pine Camp pedigree and Paul Smiths quiet; caveat—real tea stain and modest depth temper towsports appeal.

lakes.name: Lake of the Isles (Wellesley Is.)
lakes.clarity: St. Lawrence-clear, warmest water on the river
lakes.motors: NYS/river rules; ski legal in calm protected basin
lakes.blurb: Sheltered river lagoon with state-park shores; caveat—it's the St. Lawrence, not a private forest lake.

lakes.name: Mountain View + Indian (Duane)
lakes.clarity: Sandy, moderately clear
lakes.blurb: Two connected sandy lakes totaling ~540 acres, deeply quiet and cheap; caveat—each basin under 300 acres.

lakes.name: Lake Placid
lakes.clarity: Oligotrophic, superb clarity (CSLAP)
lakes.blurb: Whiteface-view masterpiece that fails one test: no realistic ≤$2.5M compound path—entry camps start well above budget.

lakes.name: Lake Dunmore
lakes.clarity: Clear mesotrophic; Secchi ~5.5–6.5 m; 105 ft deep; milfoil actively managed (DEC LMP)
lakes.motors: Unrestricted HP; traditional ski/tube statewide-exempt; on DEC 2026 wakesports-zone list
lakes.blurb: Moosalamoo/GMNF wall of forest, real ski water, best drive-to-quality ratio; summer-busy shore and thin inventory.

lakes.name: Crystal Lake (Barton)
lakes.clarity: Oligo-mesotrophic; Secchi ~6 m; 106 ft deep (DEC bathymetry); small milfoil population under treatment
lakes.motors: Unrestricted HP; DEC wakesports zone designated
lakes.blurb: Cliff-walled, deep and clear with true camp stock; Rt 5 west shore and village parks at north end temper it.

lakes.name: Harvey's Lake (Barnet)
lakes.clarity: Meso-oligotrophic; ~140 ft deep; Secchi ~5.5–6.5 m; Cousteau's first dive; healthy native plants (VPR/DEC)
lakes.motors: Motors unrestricted, high-speed legal (UPW table); DEC wakesports zone
lakes.blurb: The small-gem exception: deep, clear, hushed West Barnet, closest NEK water; 351 ac means modest ski room.

lakes.name: Little Averill Pond
lakes.clarity: Oligotrophic reference-grade; Secchi ~7 m+; loon nesting lake
lakes.motors: Unrestricted; DEC wakesports zone designated (2026 list)
lakes.blurb: Wildest clear water on this list; 7-hour edge, rough camp roads, almost no market—patience play beside Great Averill.

lakes.name: Lake Fairlee
lakes.clarity: Mesotrophic; Secchi starts high, declines through summer; internal P loading noted (DEC LMP 2023)
lakes.motors: Unrestricted; NOT on 2026 wakesports list (trad ski/tube still legal)
lakes.blurb: Forested, quiet, 4:40 out, youth-camp culture; squeaks the size bar and clarity is good-not-great.

lakes.name: Island Pond (Brighton)
lakes.clarity: Mesotrophic; Secchi ~4.5–5 m; forested south/east shores, state park
lakes.blurb: Big cheap water with Brighton SP forest; village, rail line and middling clarity keep it off the podium.

lakes.name: Lake Salem (Derby)
lakes.clarity: Mesotrophic; Secchi ~4–5 m; milfoil-prevention program active; occasional bloom notices
lakes.blurb: Serious acreage and one true compound listing; Rt 105 shore, Derby sprawl and softer water are the caveats.

lakes.name: Lake Morey
lakes.clarity: Mesotrophic, alum-treated (35-ft wakesports floor protects treatment); Secchi ~4.5 m
lakes.motors: 40 mph cap (UPW table)—skiing fine; DEC wakesports zone
lakes.blurb: Closest legal ski water with a zone; cottage-ringed resort lake, engineered water quality—not the forested archetype.

listings.name: Webb Lake build parcel — $985K
listings.fit: Build the sketch from scratch; lodge near shore, cabins beyond the 250-ft zone

listings.name: 215 Judson Rd — $1.2M
listings.fit: Archetype lake; logistics are the debate

listings.name: LaCross Ln compound — $1.2M
listings.fit: Lake VIEWS confirmed, frontage NOT — pair with a frontage parcel below

listings.name: Two-cabin property — $649K
listings.fit: A compound seed on the Great Camp lake

listings.name: Private cove — $599K
listings.fit: Pair with an adjacent camp for a sub-$2M compound

listings.name: Pine Point Lodge, U. St. Regis — $2.6M
listings.fit: Turnkey stretch; guideboat culture, small lake for wake sports

listings.name: Hamlin Bay parcels — $1.38M
listings.fit: Passes APA math for lodge + 5 cabins outright; tea-stained water

listings.name: Six-cabin colony, Gt. Sacandaga — $2.5M
listings.fit: Turnkey program, wrong-culture lake — the program-first fallback

listings.name: Panther Cove — $3.7M (benchmark)
listings.fit: Over budget — tour it to calibrate what done looks like

listings.name: 657 Bemis Rd — $725K (edge)
listings.detail: 53.9 ac · house + new barn · ~7 h drive
listings.fit: The over-the-line bargain; verify exact frontage

listings.name: Ferry Point lodge, 13BR/250' — $3.0M
listings.fit: Turnkey lodge sleeping all five couples day one; add bunkhouses later

listings.name: 107 Cotton Hill Rd — $1.42M
listings.fit: Acreage to add cabins; rare land depth here

listings.name: 58 Lower Bay Rd — $1.33M

rentals.name: Bluff Point Camp — boat-access, sleeps 18
rentals.detail: Main cabin sleeps 10 plus a guest cottage for 4+; 6BR/4BA, max 18; two private docks that fit six boats; boat-access only; $4,500/wk June–October. 3742 Bluff Point.
rentals.fit: Six bedrooms and room for six boats on the Great Camp lake for $560 a couple. The boat-in logistics are the whole debate — the same debate as the Big Moose listing in the purchase brief. By-owner listing, no platform fee.

rentals.name: Camp Garçon — historic Great Camp, 7 BR but capped at 10
rentals.detail: Seven bedrooms, two baths, porch, fire pit and dock — but the owner caps occupancy at 10. $4,545/wk, Friday to Friday.
rentals.fit: Passes the bedroom test and fails the couples test: the occupancy cap is a rule, not a suggestion. Listed so you can ask whether they would consider 16 for a known group; otherwise a benchmark for what a real Great Camp rents for.

rentals.name: Covewood Lodge — Great Camp inn with 18 cottages
rentals.rateNote: main lodge ~$2,330/wk peak; cottages priced individually
rentals.detail: Historic 1928 main lodge (two 2BR apartments, rooms; peak weekly ~$2,330) plus 18–19 cottages from 1 to ~6 bedrooms; weekly in peak season; beach, docks, boats. (800) 357-7530.
rentals.fit: The whole-camp buyout on the hushed classic: take the main lodge and three or four of the big cottages and eight couples have a Great Camp to themselves. Book direct — Covewood has never been on a platform.
rentals.season: Weekly late June to Labor Day; 3-night minimum otherwise

rentals.name: Quisisana — 42 cottages, full American plan, music every night
rentals.rateNote: full American plan; group terms on request
rentals.detail: Since 1917: 42 private cottages (1–3 BR) and a 7-room lodge on Kezar's shore; rates include three meals a day and nightly chamber music, opera and musical theatre performed by the conservatory-student staff. Owned by the Orans family since 1984.
rentals.fit: No single house on Kezar sleeps sixteen — the market is too thin — so the eight-couple answer is a block of cottages here. It is also the best way to spend a week on the truest Squam analog while the group decides whether to spend twenty years on it.

rentals.name: Seymour Lake Lodge — take all 7 rooms and 3 apartments
rentals.detail: Year-round lodge on the shore at 28 Valley Road: 7 guest rooms plus 3 apartments, communal kitchen, game room, beach, dock, free canoes, kayaks and boats. Rooms $95–155/night. 802-895-2563.
rentals.fit: A buyout here is ten doors for roughly $1,200 a night for the whole building — cheap enough that the group can test the Northeast Kingdom without commitment. It is an inn, not an estate: shared kitchen, lodge culture. Priced like it.

rentals.name: Largest private rental on Seymour — 5 BR, sleeps 9
rentals.detail: The biggest single property found: main house (3BR) plus a two-bedroom en-suite guest cottage on 35 acres with 1,000 ft of private shore and a lakeside dock. Sleeps 9.
rentals.fit: Included so the map is honest: Seymour's private rental stock tops out at five bedrooms. Eight couples here means the lodge buyout above, or two adjacent VRBOs.

rentals.name: Lake Front Life — sleeps 16, dock for 16+, theatre room
rentals.detail: Listed as the premium rental on Parker Pond: sleeps 16, private dock sized for the whole group, hot tub, theatre room, six kayaks; from ~$1,215/night. Bedroom count not published in search results.
rentals.fit: On the clearest of Maine's four standouts. If the bedroom count is seven or more, this is the Northeast's best single-house answer at about $1,060 a couple for the week. Confirm bedrooms before anything else.

rentals.name: Silver Lake — no 7+ BR rental found
rentals.detail: Largest waterfront rental found: a 5BR/2BA that sleeps 12 with a dock (bring your own boat, four kayaks). Nothing at 7+ bedrooms surfaced.
rentals.fit: Honest answer: Silver Lake's rental stock is family-cottage scale. Eight couples means two adjacent houses, or Purity Spring Resort on the next lake over.

rentals.name: Echo Lake — no group rental found
rentals.detail: The only rental found is a 2BR camp with a dock and boat that sleeps 6. Echo is a private-camp lake with almost no rental market.
rentals.fit: Nothing here for eight couples. Rent on Parker Pond ten minutes away and boat both.
